title: Scale cocycles, finite scheme changes and controlled RG equations

items.title: Formal scaling and renormalization cocycle
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice.

Let $\mathbb M=\mathbb R^4$ have Minkowski metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. A scalar local polynomial functional is a finite sum
$$F(\phi)=c+\sum_{j=1}^{N}\int_{\mathbb M} f_j(x)P_j(j^{s_j}\phi(x))\,d^4x,$$
where $N$ is a finite nonnegative integer, $\phi\in C^\infty(\mathbb M;\mathbb R)$, $c\in\mathbb C$, and $f_j\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb M;\mathbb C)$. For a finite integer $s_j\ge0$, the $s_j$-jet is $j^{s_j}\phi(x)=(\partial^\alpha\phi(x))_{\alpha\in\{0,1,2,\ldots\}^4,\,|\alpha|\le s_j}$; each $P_j$ is a complex polynomial in these finitely many jet coordinates. This is the local functional class used by the supplied scalar time-ordered system.

For every mass label $m\ge0$, suppose a normalized scalar time-ordered system $T_n^{(m)}$ with the same local scalar contract is supplied. Define its coefficientwise formal S-map by
$$\mathcal S_m(V)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n!}T_n^{(m)}(V,\ldots,V),\qquad T_0^{(m)}=1,\quad T_1^{(m)}=\operatorname{id}.$$
The series is formal in the interaction degree; no analytic convergence is asserted.

Use units $c=\hbar=1$, so the mass label $m$ has mass dimension one. The scale parameter $\rho>0$ is dimensionless. On scalar field configurations put
$$(C_\rho\phi)(x)=\rho^{-1}\phi(\rho^{-1}x),$$
the engineering scaling of a four-dimensional scalar field. On a family of mass-labelled functionals or maps $A=(A_m)_{m\ge0}$, define
$$(\sigma_\rho A)_m=C_\rho^*(A_{\rho^{-1}m}),\qquad (C_\rho^*F)(\phi)=F(C_{\rho^{-1}}\phi).$$
Extend this action coefficientwise to formal series and maps. It obeys $\sigma_1=\operatorname{id}$ and $\sigma_{\rho\tau}=\sigma_\rho\sigma_\tau$; the mass label scales as $m\mapsto\rho m$. The dilation sends compact supports to compact supports and normalizes the proper orthochronous Poincare action.

Assume for each $\rho>0$ that $\mathcal S$ and its scale conjugate $\sigma_\rho\mathcal S\sigma_\rho^{-1}$ are both normalized scalar time-ordered systems for the same mass-indexed free data after the stated mass relabelling. Define $Z_\rho$ to be the unique formal local map with identity linear term satisfying
$$\sigma_\rho\mathcal S\sigma_\rho^{-1}=\mathcal S\circ Z_\rho.$$
Here $Z_\rho(V)=V+O(V^2)$ means that all terms after the linear term have interaction degree at least two. This is a conditional definition: no existence of a time-ordered system for any particular model is asserted.

items.title: Scaling yields the twisted composition law
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice.

Let $Z_\rho$ be the mass-indexed formal renormalization map defined for the scale action $\sigma_\rho$, $\rho>0$. For all $\rho,\tau>0$,
$$Z_{\rho\tau}=Z_\rho\circ\bigl(\sigma_\rho Z_\tau\sigma_\rho^{-1}\bigr).$$
If conjugation by every $\sigma_\rho$ acts trivially on the renormalization subgroup, this reduces to $Z_{\rho\tau}=Z_\rho\circ Z_\tau$. In the general mass-dependent case the twisted formula is the claim; no one-parameter subgroup law is asserted.

items.title: One-coupling truncated RG flow and scheme invariance
items.statement:
Let $t=\log\rho\in\mathbb R$ be the dimensionless logarithmic scale parameter associated with $\rho>0$. Take $g(t)$ to be a dimensionless real coupling, and prescribe dimensionless constants $b,g_0\in\mathbb R$ in the truncated scalar initial-value problem
$$\frac{dg}{dt}=bg^2,\qquad g(0)=g_0.$$
If $c:=bg_0=0$, its unique maximal real solution is $g(t)=g_0$ on $\mathbb R$. If $c\ne0$, its unique maximal solution through $t=0$ is
$$g(t)=\frac{g_0}{1-bg_0t}$$
on $(-\infty,c^{-1})$ when $c>0$ and on $(c^{-1},\infty)$ when $c<0$.

For the formal beta series $\beta(g)=bg^2+O(g^3)$, let $\widetilde g=\Phi(g)=g+ag^2+O(g^3)$ be an invertible formal change of dimensionless coupling, with dimensionless $a\in\mathbb R$. Here $O(g^k)$ denotes a formal power series whose terms have degree at least $k$, and $\Phi'$ is the termwise formal derivative. The transformed vector field is
$$\widetilde\beta(\widetilde g)=\bigl(\Phi'(g)\beta(g)\bigr)\big|_{g=\Phi^{-1}(\widetilde g)}.$$
Its quadratic coefficient is $b$. The real ODE is exact only for the displayed truncation; neither it nor the formal scheme-change statement determines $b$ from a QFT graph or bounds omitted higher-order terms. Its pole is a property of this truncated equation, not a theorem about an ultraviolet completion.

items.title: A truncated Landau pole is not continuum nonexistence
items.statement: For dimensionless $b>0$ and $g_0>0$, the truncated equation $dg/dt=bg^2$ with $g(0)=g_0$ has maximal solution $g(t)=g_0/(1-bg_0t)$ for $t<t_*:=(bg_0)^{-1}$, and $g(t)\to+\infty$ as $t\uparrow t_*$. This is a divergence of the exact solution to the stated truncated equation. The calculation supplies no estimate for omitted higher-order beta terms near $t_*$ and implies no nonexistence result for a continuum theory.
